channel.title: Finance
channel.description: Latest investing news and finance headlines straight from Wall Street.

item.title: Uber partners with China's Pony.ai for 2,000 robotaxis in Europe
item.description: The rollout comes as robotaxi fleet sizes become increasingly critical for commercialization.

item.title: These charts show why stocks keep rallying. Profit margins are the highest on record
item.description: Recent FactSet data show that the rise in earnings is not coming from sales growth alone.

item.title: 'Big Short' investor Steve Eisman sees an Achilles' heel in the AI boom
item.description: Steve Eisman is warning that the artificial intelligence boom has become increasingly dependent on the fortunes of just two companies: OpenAI and Anthropic.

item.title: Iran looks to ramp up economic alliance with BRICS nations as war with U.S. drags on
item.description: Iran’s central bank chief said Thursday that the country is set to join the BRICS New Development Bank.

item.title: This Chinese firm has topped Micron and Kioxia in shipments of crucial NAND memory chips
item.description: Counterpoint Research looked at the NAND segment of memory chips, which is benefitting along with the larger DRAM segment from artificial intelligence demand.

item.title: SpaceX short sellers are running out of bullets as stock rebounds more than 40% off low
item.description: Short interest in SpaceX fell to about 11% of the company's publicly traded shares Wednesday, down sharply from a peak of 34% last week, according to S3.

item.title: New York City Council announces probe into prediction market platforms’ marketing strategies
item.description: In letters to four prediction market platforms, City Council Speaker Julie Menin said the council was also actively considering legislation to address concerns.

item.title: EVs dominate China’s car market: 5 takeaways from the country's latest auto sales data
item.description: The China Passenger Car Association released data Tuesday showing penetration of new energy vehicles rose in July. Tesla's Model Y remained popular.

item.title: Why Jensen Huang’s $500 billion AI financing plan faces a big risk from China
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is pitching GPUs as long-term collateral to unlock $500 billion in funding. The question is how fast will his chips depreciate?

item.title: Is betting on elections using prediction markets illegal? Many states are unsure as midterms approach
item.description: Twenty-three states have laws banning betting on elections, according to Pew Research. Not every state is sure these rules apply to prediction market trades.

item.title: AI computing power is becoming a tradable asset class as CME launches futures contracts
item.description: The exchange is partnering with Silicon Data to introduce two compute futures contracts on Oct. 5, pending regulatory review.

item.title: Why JPMorgan is investing big in the 2028 LA Olympics
item.description: JPMorgan is making a nine-figure bet as the Olympics Games' first-ever global banking partner.

item.title: Polymarket makes moves to get house in order before expected boom times for prediction markets this fall
item.description: The marketing changes come amid an investigation by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission into the company's promotional practices.

item.title: Wall Street just endorsed Jensen Huang's 'big concept' for AI. What now?
item.description: The first three-plus years of the AI build-out have been funded by record amounts of equity and debt issued by leading tech companies. Nvidia has a new idea.

item.title: Nvidia lines up $500 billion in financing as CEO Jensen Huang tells CNBC his chips are ‘investable asset’
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that because its hardware is broadly adopted, flexible and transferable, lenders can underwrite compute as revenue-generating.

item.title: Three reasons Goldman's co-head of global banking and markets says to stay invested
item.description: Goldman Sachs' Ashok Varadhan pointed to three reasons for his constructive outlook.

item.title: Next big push in ETF industry? Why these risk assets are gaining traction as interest rate uncertainty persists
item.description: Collateralized loan obligations may become the next big push in the exchange-traded fund industry.

item.title: Berkshire earnings rose last quarter and CEO Greg Abel is starting to deploy Buffett's massive cash hoard
item.description: Strength across its energy, railroad and manufacturing businesses more than offset weaker insurance results.

item.title: Odds the Fed will hike in September tumble following big July jobs miss
item.description: A weaker labor market would weaken the case for raising rates, which some members of the central bank have called for amid higher energy prices.

item.title: Copper jumps to its highest level ever. What the metal is telling us
item.description: Once a reliable gauge if economic health, "Dr. Copper" may be giving complicated signals this year.

item.title: United Wholesale Mortgage plunges 35% after suspending dividend and raising capital
item.description: "We're taking decisive action to make UWM stronger, more liquid and better positioned to win for years to come," CEO Mat Ishbia said in a statement.

item.title: Traders on Kalshi now think it's likely that the S&P 500 will hit 8,000 in 2026
item.description: The rise in odds come after the broad index hit record highs in a more than 5% four-day rally that ended Wednesday.

item.title: Fed Governor Cook says she's 'prepared to act' on rate hike to address inflation
item.description: Cook was part of a 9-3 majority that voted last week to keep the central bank's benchmark borrowing rate in a range between 3.5%-3.75%.

item.title: As Warsh and the Fed contemplate fewer meetings, markets brace for potential volatility ahead
item.description: Since taking office in May, Warsh has implemented several measures that reverse decades of Fed culture.

item.title: Bank of America spends $250 million a year on GLP-1 drugs for its employees, CEO says
item.description: Employers have grappled with soaring demand for GLP-1 drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy, which can cost thousands of dollars per patient annually.

item.title: Situational Awareness hedge fund meltdown was a warning shot for leveraged markets, BofA CEO says
item.description: Bank of America was among the prime brokers for the hedge fund, which is run by Leopold Aschenbrenner.

item.title: Ken Griffin's Citadel posts best month in years after scooping up Situational Awareness stocks
item.description: The July gains came after Citadel acquired the bulk of the public-stock portfolio formerly held by Situational Awareness late last month.

item.title: Michael Burry bets against rally: 'We are near a major top, and possible a 1987-type fall'
item.description: "I continue to believe it is possible we are near a major top, and possible a 1987-type fall," Burry said in a Tuesday Substack post.

item.title: Polymarket in talks for fundraising round at more than $20 billion valuation
item.description: The reports come after the company told CNBC in June that its annualized revenue was well above $1 billion.

item.title: Philadelphia Fed President Paulson content with rates at current level, but keeping an open mind
item.description: Paulson said voting with the majority last week wasn't a tough decision.
